source.text: Ἐν δὲ ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις πληθυνόντων τῶν μαθητῶν ἐγένετο γογγυσμὸς τῶν Ἑλληνιστῶν πρὸς τοὺς Ἑβραίους ὅτι παρεθεωροῦντο ἐν τῇ διακονίᾳ τῇ καθημερινῇ αἱ χῆραι αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: In now the days these, multiplying the disciples, there arose a grumbling of the Hellenists against the Hebrews, because were being overlooked in the serving the daily the widows of them.

en.L: Now in these days, as the disciples were multiplying, there arose a grumbling of the Hellenists against the Hebrews, because their widows were being overlooked in the daily serving.
en.B: In those days, while the number of disciples kept growing, the Greek-speaking believers began to grumble against those who spoke Hebrew. Their widows, they said, were being passed over when food was given out each day.
en.R: During this time more and more people became followers of Jesus. Some of them spoke Greek, and others spoke the language of the Jews in Judea. The Greek speakers began to complain about the others. Every day food was handed out to widows, but the Greek-speaking widows were being left out.

decisions.choice: Hellenists and Hebrews: two groups of Jewish believers, set apart mainly by language
decisions.reason: Both groups were Jews; the first Gentile believers come later (10:1-48, 11:20). The names point most clearly to language: the Hellenists spoke Greek, and many had come to Jerusalem from Jewish communities abroad (2:5-11, 6:9); the Hebrews spoke Hebrew or Aramaic, the language of the Jews of the land (21:40, 22:2). Whatever else divided them, the text says only that the complaint ran along this line.

decisions.choice: the daily serving: a share of food given each day to widows in need
decisions.reason: The believers shared what they had with anyone in need (2:44-45, 4:34-35). Widows often had no one to provide for them, and the law told Israel to care for them (Deuteronomy 14:29; 24:19-21). Serving at tables in 6:2 shows that food was being given out.

decisions.choice: serving: the work of serving, here the handing out of food
decisions.reason: The same word is used for the apostles' "service of the word" in 6:4, and its verb for serving at tables in 6:2. Luke sets the two kinds of service side by side.

decisions.choice: disciples: the believers in Jesus
decisions.reason: This is the first time Acts calls the whole community "disciples", learners who follow a teacher; the word is used of all believers from here on (6:7, 9:1, 11:26).

decisions.choice: were being overlooked: passed over again and again
decisions.reason: The verb is in the imperfect, for something that kept happening. It does not say whether the neglect was deliberate.

decisions.choice: the Greek-speaking believers; those who spoke Hebrew
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the names mean, as the meaning note explains; Literal keeps the names.

decisions.choice: food was given out each day
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what was being served, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: προσκαλεσάμενοι δὲ οἱ δώδεκα τὸ πλῆθος τῶν μαθητῶν εἶπαν· Οὐκ ἀρεστόν ἐστιν ἡμᾶς καταλείψαντας τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ διακονεῖν τραπέζαις·

records.literal_gloss: Having called together then the Twelve the multitude of the disciples said, Not pleasing it is [for] us having left the word of the God to serve tables.

en.L: And the Twelve, having called together the multitude of the disciples, said, "It is not pleasing [for] us, having left the word of God, to serve tables.
en.B: So the Twelve called the whole company of the disciples together and said, "It is not fitting for us to leave aside the word of God in order to serve at tables.
en.R: So the twelve apostles called all the followers of Jesus together. They said, "We should not stop teaching God's message so that we can hand out food.

decisions.choice: the Twelve: the apostles, with Matthias in Judas's place
decisions.reason: Luke calls the apostles "the Twelve" (Luke 6:13, 9:1). Their number was made whole again in 1:26.

decisions.choice: not pleasing: not right or fitting, not what God wants
decisions.reason: The word means acceptable or pleasing. The apostles do not look down on serving food; they say it is not their part to leave the word for it (6:4).

decisions.choice: serve tables: hand out the food for the daily share
alternatives: keep money tables, as bankers did
decisions.reason: "Tables" here goes with the daily serving of food in 6:1. The verb is the one from which the noun for "serving" comes, so the apostles set this serving beside the service of the word (6:4).

decisions.choice: the word of God: God's message about Jesus, which the apostles preached and taught
decisions.reason: As in 4:31, the word of God is the message the apostles were sent to speak (1:8).

decisions.choice: hand out food
decisions.reason: Readable says what serving tables meant here.

decisions.choice: teaching God's message
decisions.reason: Readable says what leaving the word would mean: no longer teaching it.

source.text: ἐπισκέψασθε δέ, ἀδελφοί, ἄνδρας ἐξ ὑμῶν μαρτυρουμένους ἑπτὰ πλήρεις πνεύματος καὶ σοφίας, οὓς καταστήσομεν ἐπὶ τῆς χρείας ταύτης·

records.literal_gloss: Select but, brothers, men from you being well spoken of seven, full of Spirit and of wisdom, whom we will appoint over the need this;

en.L: So select, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, seven men from among you who are well spoken of, full of [the] Spirit and of wisdom, whom we will appoint over this need.
en.B: So, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, look among yourselves for seven men of good reputation, full of the Spirit and of wisdom, and we will put them in charge of this need.
en.R: So, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, choose seven men from your group. Everyone must know that they are good men. They must be filled with the Holy Spirit and with wisdom. We will give them this job.

decisions.choice: brothers: the whole community of disciples, men and women
decisions.reason: The apostles speak to "the multitude of the disciples" (6:2), and the choice was made by "the whole multitude" (6:5).

decisions.choice: men: the seven were to be men
decisions.reason: The word means adult males, not people in general, so it stays "men"; the address to the community before it takes in everyone.

decisions.choice: well spoken of: known and approved by others
decisions.reason: The verb means to be witnessed to; others vouch for them (compare 10:22, 16:2).

decisions.choice: Spirit: the Holy Spirit
alternatives: a human spirit, a spirited character
decisions.reason: Stephen is said in 6:5 to be full of the Holy Spirit, and the believers had been filled with the Spirit (2:4, 4:31).

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "full of the Spirit"
alternatives: some manuscripts read "full of the Holy Spirit"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, add "holy", perhaps from 6:5. The sense is the same. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: this need: the task of meeting the widows' need
decisions.reason: The word means a need, and so the work that meets it. The text gives the seven a task, not a title.

decisions.choice: brothers and sisters, with "brothers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The address takes in the whole community, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: short sentences: everyone must know they are good men; filled with the Holy Spirit and with wisdom
alternatives: well spoken of, full of the Spirit and of wisdom
decisions.reason: Readable breaks up the description and names the Holy Spirit, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: ἡμεῖς δὲ τῇ προσευχῇ καὶ τῇ διακονίᾳ τοῦ λόγου προσκαρτερήσομεν.

records.literal_gloss: We but to the prayer and to the service of the word will devote ourselves.

en.L: But we will devote ourselves to prayer and to the service of the word."
en.B: As for us, we will hold fast to prayer and to the service of the word."
en.R: Then we can keep giving our time to prayer and to teaching God's message."

decisions.choice: the service of the word: preaching and teaching God's message
decisions.reason: The noun is the one used for the daily serving of food in 6:1. Both are service; the apostles keep to the one they were given.

decisions.choice: devote ourselves: keep on steadily at something
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 1:14 and 2:42, of the believers holding fast to prayer and to the apostles' teaching.

decisions.choice: prayer: prayer, both shared and private
alternatives: the temple's set hours of prayer only
decisions.reason: The word has the article, "the prayer", as in 2:42. It may include the set times of prayer (3:1), but is not limited to them.

decisions.choice: hold fast to
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the verb means: holding to something without letting go.

decisions.choice: teaching God's message
decisions.reason: Readable says what the service of the word was, as at 6:2.

source.text: καὶ ἤρεσεν ὁ λόγος ἐνώπιον παντὸς τοῦ πλήθους, καὶ ἐξελέξαντο Στέφανον, ἄνδρα πλήρης πίστεως καὶ πνεύματος ἁγίου, καὶ Φίλιππον καὶ Πρόχορον καὶ Νικάνορα καὶ Τίμωνα καὶ Παρμενᾶν καὶ Νικόλαον προσήλυτον Ἀντιοχέα, οὓς ἔστησαν ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀποστόλων, καὶ προσευξάμενοι ἐπέθηκαν αὐτοῖς τὰς χεῖρας.

records.literal_gloss: And pleased the word before all the multitude, and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of Spirit Holy, and Philip and Prochorus and Nicanor and Timon and Parmenas and Nicolaus a proselyte of Antioch, \v 6 whom they set before the apostles, and having prayed they laid on them the hands.

en.L: And the word pleased the whole multitude, and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of [the] Holy Spirit, and Philip and Prochorus and Nicanor and Timon and Parmenas and Nicolaus, a proselyte of Antioch, \v 6 whom they set before the apostles, and having prayed, they laid [their] hands on them.
en.B: The whole gathering approved of what was said. They chose Stephen, a man full of faith and the Holy Spirit, together with Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolaus, a convert to Judaism from Antioch. \v 6 They had these men stand before the apostles, and after praying, they laid their hands on them.
en.R: Everyone liked this plan. They chose Stephen, who had great faith and was full of the Holy Spirit. They also chose Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolaus. Nicolaus was from the city of Antioch. He was not born a Jew, but he had become one. \v 6 The people brought these seven men to the apostles. Then they prayed and put their hands on the seven men.

decisions.choice: seven Greek names
decisions.reason: All seven names are Greek. Many Jews of the day had Greek names, so this does not prove that every one of the seven was a Greek-speaking Jew, but it suggests that the community chose men from the side that had complained (6:1).

decisions.choice: a proselyte of Antioch: a Gentile from Antioch who had become a Jew
decisions.reason: A proselyte was a Gentile who took on the law of Moses and joined the Jewish people (2:10). Nicolaus came from Antioch in Syria, where the good news would soon be preached to Gentiles (11:19-26).

decisions.choice: the seven: not called deacons here
decisions.reason: The text gives the seven a task (6:3), not a title. Later the church had "deacons", from the same family of words as "serving" (Philippians 1:1; 1 Timothy 3:8-13), but Acts does not name the seven so, and what follows does not settle how later church offices began. In 21:8 Philip is called "one of the seven"; Stephen and Philip are soon preaching (6:8-10, 8:5).

decisions.choice: laid their hands on them: a sign of being set apart and sent with blessing for a task
decisions.reason: Moses laid his hands on Joshua to give him his charge (Numbers 27:18-23). In Acts the laying on of hands goes with prayer when people are sent out for God's work (13:3).

decisions.choice: who prayed and laid on hands: the apostles, or the whole gathering
decisions.reason: The sentence does not change its subject, so it could be the community; but the apostles had said they would appoint the seven (6:3), so they may be meant.

decisions.choice: the word: what the apostles said, their proposal
decisions.reason: Here the word means the apostles' speech in 6:2-4.

decisions.choice: Nicolaus
decisions.reason: The spelling follows the Greek form of the name.

decisions.choice: he was not born a Jew, but he had become one
decisions.reason: Readable says what a proselyte was.

source.text: Καὶ ὁ λόγος τοῦ θεοῦ ηὔξανεν, καὶ ἐπληθύνετο ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν μαθητῶν ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ σφόδρα, πολύς τε ὄχλος τῶν ἱερέων ὑπήκουον τῇ πίστει.

records.literal_gloss: And the word of the God was growing, and was being multiplied the number of the disciples in Jerusalem greatly, a great and crowd of the priests were obeying the faith.

en.L: And the word of God kept growing, and the number of the disciples in Jerusalem kept multiplying greatly, and a great crowd of the priests were obeying the faith.
en.B: So God's word went on spreading. In Jerusalem the disciples grew greatly in number, and large numbers of priests were coming to obey the faith.
en.R: So more and more people heard God's message. The number of followers of Jesus in Jerusalem grew very large. Many priests also obeyed the faith and believed in Jesus.

decisions.choice: the word of God kept growing: the message spread and took hold
decisions.reason: Luke speaks of the word as a living thing that grows (12:24, 19:20), as seed grows in Jesus's parable (Luke 8:11-15).

decisions.choice: obeying the faith: believing the message about Jesus and living by it
alternatives: keeping the rules of the priesthood
decisions.reason: Here "the faith" is what the believers believed and trusted; to obey it is to accept it and follow it (compare Romans 1:5, 16:26).

decisions.choice: priests: ordinary priests who served in the temple by turns
decisions.reason: There were many priests, serving in the temple in divisions (Luke 1:5, 1:8-9). These were not the chief priests, who had opposed the apostles (4:1-6, 5:17).

decisions.choice: and believed in Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable adds what obeying the faith meant, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: more and more people heard God's message
alternatives: the word of God kept growing
decisions.reason: Readable says what the word growing meant.

source.text: Στέφανος δὲ πλήρης χάριτος καὶ δυνάμεως ἐποίει τέρατα καὶ σημεῖα μεγάλα ἐν τῷ λαῷ.

records.literal_gloss: Stephen now full of grace and of power was doing wonders and signs great among the people.

en.L: And Stephen, full of grace and power, was doing great wonders and signs among the people.
en.B: Stephen was full of grace and power, and he worked wonders and great signs among the people.
en.R: God's grace and power filled Stephen. He did amazing wonders and signs among the people.

decisions.choice: grace: God's gracious favor, at work in him
decisions.reason: The word can mean favor that people show (2:47) as well as God's grace. Set beside "power", it points to God's grace given to Stephen, as in 4:33, where great power and great grace go together.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "full of grace"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, read "faith", likely from 6:5. Earlier manuscripts have "grace". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: wonders and signs: miracles that amaze and that point to God at work
decisions.reason: The pair is used of what God did through Jesus (2:22) and through the apostles (2:43, 5:12). This is the first time it is used of someone outside the Twelve.

decisions.choice: God's grace
decisions.reason: Readable names whose grace it was, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: ἀνέστησαν δέ τινες τῶν ἐκ τῆς συναγωγῆς τῆς λεγομένης Λιβερτίνων καὶ Κυρηναίων καὶ Ἀλεξανδρέων καὶ τῶν ἀπὸ Κιλικίας καὶ Ἀσίας συζητοῦντες τῷ Στεφάνῳ, καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυον ἀντιστῆναι τῇ σοφίᾳ καὶ τῷ πνεύματι ᾧ ἐλάλει.

records.literal_gloss: Rose up but some of those from the synagogue the called of Freedmen and of Cyrenians and of Alexandrians and of those from Cilicia and Asia, disputing with Stephen, \v 10 and not they were able to withstand the wisdom and the Spirit by which he was speaking.

en.L: But some of those from the synagogue called [the synagogue] of [the] Freedmen, and of Cyrenians and of Alexandrians, and of those from Cilicia and Asia, rose up, disputing with Stephen, \v 10 and they were not able to withstand the wisdom and the Spirit with which he was speaking.
en.B: Then opposition rose up from the synagogue known as the Freedmen's, with Cyrenians and Alexandrians and people from Cilicia and Asia, and they began debating with Stephen. \v 10 Yet the wisdom and the Spirit with which he spoke were too much for them; they could not hold their ground.
en.R: Some Jews belonged to a meeting place called the Synagogue of the Freedmen. Others came from the cities of Cyrene and Alexandria in Africa, and from the lands of Cilicia and Asia. These men stood up and started arguing with Stephen. \v 10 But when Stephen spoke, the Holy Spirit gave him wisdom. They could not win the argument against him.

decisions.choice: the synagogue of the Freedmen: a synagogue of Jews who had been slaves, or whose families had been
decisions.reason: A freedman was a slave who had been set free. Many Jews were taken to Rome as captives after the Romans took Jerusalem in 63 BC, and many were later freed. Such people, or their descendants, could have had their own synagogue in Jerusalem. A Greek inscription found in Jerusalem tells of a synagogue built for reading the law and housing visitors from abroad; it shows such synagogues existed, though it cannot be tied to this one.

decisions.choice: how many synagogues: one, or two or more
alternatives: a separate synagogue for each group
decisions.reason: The Greek can be read as one synagogue whose members came from all these places, or as the Freedmen's synagogue with others beside it. The words do not settle it, and the renderings keep the list as it stands.

decisions.choice: Cyrene, Alexandria, Cilicia and Asia: places with large Jewish communities
decisions.reason: Cyrene was a city in North Africa, west of Egypt (Simon came from there, Luke 23:26). Alexandria was the great city of Egypt. Cilicia lay in the southeast of what is now Turkey; its city Tarsus was Saul's home (21:39), and Saul appears in 7:58. Asia was the Roman province in the west of what is now Turkey, with Ephesus as its chief city (2:9).

decisions.choice: they could not withstand his wisdom: as Jesus promised
decisions.reason: Jesus promised his followers "a mouth and wisdom" that none of their opponents would be able to withstand (Luke 21:15). The verb is the same.

decisions.choice: the Spirit: the Holy Spirit, by whom he spoke
decisions.reason: Stephen was "full of the Spirit and of wisdom" (6:3, 6:5), and the Spirit gives words to speak (Luke 12:12). The word could mean his own spirit or manner, but the Holy Spirit fits the chapter best.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: the sentence ends here
alternatives: a few manuscripts add that they were refuted by him with all boldness
decisions.reason: One early Greek manuscript and some early translations add a longer sentence saying that Stephen's opponents could not face the truth and were refuted by him. The addition is not found in most manuscripts. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the cities of Cyrene and Alexandria in Africa; the lands of Cilicia and Asia
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of places these were.

decisions.choice: the Holy Spirit gave him wisdom; they could not win the argument
alternatives: they could not withstand the wisdom and the Spirit with which he spoke
decisions.reason: Readable puts the Spirit first and says what withstanding meant, as the meaning notes explain. It is a simplification of the Greek, which names wisdom and Spirit together.

source.text: τότε ὑπέβαλον ἄνδρας λέγοντας ὅτι Ἀκηκόαμεν αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ῥήματα βλάσφημα εἰς Μωϋσῆν καὶ τὸν θεόν·

records.literal_gloss: Then they secretly put forward men saying, We have heard him speaking words blasphemous against Moses and the God;

en.L: Then they secretly put forward men who said, "We have heard him speaking blasphemous words against Moses and God."
en.B: Then they quietly got some men to say, "We have heard this man utter blasphemies against Moses and against God."
en.R: So they secretly got some men to lie about Stephen. These men said, "We heard Stephen say evil things against Moses and against God!"

decisions.choice: secretly put forward: got men to speak, by arrangement behind the scenes
decisions.reason: The verb means to put someone up to something in an underhand way. The text does not say how they were persuaded.

decisions.choice: blasphemous: insulting, speaking against what is holy
decisions.reason: To blaspheme God was a crime that the law punished by death (Leviticus 24:16). Speaking against Moses meant speaking against the law God gave through him (6:13).

decisions.choice: false charges against Stephen, as against Jesus
decisions.reason: Jesus was accused of blasphemy at his trial (Luke 22:71; Mark 14:64). Luke tells Stephen's story so that it echoes his Lord's.

decisions.choice: secretly got some men to lie
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that the men were put up to it and that their charge was false (6:13).

decisions.choice: say evil things against
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for "blasphemy".

source.text: συνεκίνησάν τε τὸν λαὸν καὶ τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους καὶ τοὺς γραμματεῖς, καὶ ἐπιστάντες συνήρπασαν αὐτὸν καὶ ἤγαγον εἰς τὸ συνέδριον, ἔστησάν τε μάρτυρας ψευδεῖς λέγοντας· Ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος οὐ παύεται λαλῶν ῥήματα κατὰ τοῦ τόπου τοῦ ἁγίου καὶ τοῦ νόμου, ἀκηκόαμεν γὰρ αὐτοῦ λέγοντος ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος οὗτος καταλύσει τὸν τόπον τοῦτον καὶ ἀλλάξει τὰ ἔθη ἃ παρέδωκεν ἡμῖν Μωϋσῆς.

records.literal_gloss: They stirred up and the people and the elders and the scribes, and having come upon [him] they seized him and led [him] into the council, \v 13 they set up and witnesses false saying, The man this not ceases speaking words against the place the holy and the law; \v 14 we have heard for him saying that Jesus the Nazarene this will destroy the place this and will change the customs which handed down to us Moses.

en.L: And they stirred up the people and the elders and the scribes, and coming upon [him] they seized him and led [him] into the council, \v 13 and they set up false witnesses who said, "This man does not stop speaking words against the holy place and the law; \v 14 for we have heard him saying that this Jesus the Nazarene will destroy this place and will change the customs which Moses handed down to us."
en.B: They roused the people, the elders and the scribes. They came upon Stephen, seized him, and took him before the council. \v 13 There they put up false witnesses, who said, "This man keeps on talking against the holy place and against the law. \v 14 We heard him say that this Jesus, the Nazarene, will pull this place down and alter the customs Moses passed on to us."
en.R: They stirred up the people, and the elders and the teachers of the law, against Stephen. They came and grabbed Stephen. They took him to the Jewish council. \v 13 They brought in men to tell lies about him. These men said, "This man is always speaking against the temple, God's holy place. He speaks against the law of Moses too. \v 14 We heard him say that this Jesus from Nazareth will destroy the temple. He said that Jesus will change the ways of living that Moses gave us."

decisions.choice: the people, the elders and the scribes: the crowd and the leaders turn against the believers
decisions.reason: Until now the people had held the apostles in high regard (2:47, 5:13, 5:26). The elders were leading men of the nation, and the scribes were experts in the law of Moses; both sat on the council (4:5).

decisions.choice: the council: the Sanhedrin, the high court of the Jews in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The council was led by the high priest (7:1) and made up of chief priests, elders and scribes. Jesus and the apostles had stood before it (Luke 22:66; Acts 4:15, 5:27).

decisions.choice: the holy place, this place: the temple
decisions.reason: The council met near the temple, and "this place" points to it. Jeremiah was charged for speaking against the temple (Jeremiah 26:6-11).

decisions.choice: false witnesses, and a saying about destroying the temple, as at Jesus's trial
decisions.reason: At Jesus's trial false witnesses said he would destroy the temple (Mark 14:56-58; Matthew 26:59-61). Jesus had foretold that the temple would be torn down (Luke 21:6), and spoke of his body as the temple (John 2:19-21). The witnesses twist what may have been said.

decisions.choice: the customs Moses handed down: the law and the way of life it shaped
decisions.reason: "Customs" covers the law of Moses and the practices that grew up around it, such as circumcision (15:1, 21:21, 28:17). The charge is that Stephen attacked Israel's way of life.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "words against the holy place"
alternatives: some manuscripts read "blasphemous words against this holy place"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, add "blasphemous" (from 6:11) and "this" (from 6:14). Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: this Jesus: a scornful way of speaking
decisions.reason: The word "this" sometimes carries contempt, as the witnesses speak of a man they reject.

decisions.choice: the temple, God's holy place
decisions.reason: Readable names the temple, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: the teachers of the law
decisions.reason: Readable says what the scribes were.

decisions.choice: pull this place down
decisions.reason: The verb means to tear down a building; Balanced uses a plain word for it.

source.text: καὶ ἀτενίσαντες εἰς αὐτὸν πάντες οἱ καθεζόμενοι ἐν τῷ συνεδρίῳ εἶδον τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ὡσεὶ πρόσωπον ἀγγέλου.

records.literal_gloss: And having looked intently at him all those sitting in the council saw the face of him as [the] face of an angel.

en.L: And looking intently at him, all who were sitting in the council saw his face [was] like [the] face of an angel.
en.B: Everyone seated in the council fixed their eyes on Stephen, and they saw that his face looked like an angel's.
en.R: All the members of the council were staring at Stephen. His face looked like the face of an angel.

decisions.choice: like the face of an angel: something of heaven showed in his face
alternatives: he looked calm and innocent only
decisions.reason: The text does not say what they saw. Angels appear with shining glory (Luke 2:9, 24:4), and when Jesus prayed his face was changed (Luke 9:29). It may mean his face shone, or that God's presence and peace were plain to see.

decisions.choice: Moses's shining face
decisions.reason: Stephen is accused of speaking against Moses, and Moses's face shone after he had been with God (Exodus 34:29-35). The words do not quote that passage, so the echo is possible but not certain.

decisions.choice: looked intently: stared, fixed their eyes on him
decisions.reason: The same verb as in 1:10 and 3:4.

decisions.choice: Stephen
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name him, since the last sentence spoke of Jesus and Moses.
